content:
Francis Ngannou is a Cameroonian-French professional mixed martial artist and boxer, widely regarded as one of the most powerful punchers in combat sports history.

## Background
- Born March 5, 1986, in Batié, Cameroon
- Grew up in extreme poverty, worked in sand quarries as a child
- Emigrated to Europe at age 26, facing a dangerous journey through the Sahara Desert and Mediterranean Sea
- Initially homeless in Paris before discovering boxing

## MMA Career
- Started MMA training in 2013 at MMA Factory in Paris
- UFC debut in December 2015
- Former UFC Heavyweight Champion (2021-2023)
- Known for devastating knockout power - holds record for hardest punch recorded at UFC Performance Institute
- Notable victories include Stipe Miocic (twice), Cain Velasquez, Junior dos Santos, Alistair Overeem
- Left UFC in January 2023 after contract disputes, vacating the heavyweight title

## Boxing Transition
- Made professional boxing debut in October 2023 against Tyson Fury
- Despite losing by split decision, knocked Fury down and earned widespread respect
- Tragically lost his second boxing match to Anthony Joshua by knockout in March 2024

## Personal Life
- Founded the Francis Ngannou Foundation to help youth in Cameroon
- Advocates for fighter pay and better treatment of athletes
- Lost his 18-month-old son Kobe in 2024, a devastating personal tragedy
- Speaks multiple languages including French and English

Ngannou's story from poverty to championship glory has made him an inspiration to many, representing perseverance and the pursuit of dreams against all odds.
